items.title: Good intentions, unintended consequences: The cost of regulation
items.description: Regulation is vital for protecting consumers and building trust, but unpredictable or poorly calibrated policy changes can disrupt business economics, valuations and investment.

items.title: 10 penny stocks plunge up to 70% in three months. Do you own any?
items.description: Over the past three months, 10 penny stocks have corrected sharply, falling between 35% and 70%. These stocks were identified through a screen of companies with a market capitalisation of less than Rs 1,000 crore, a share price below Rs 20 and a minimum recent trading volume of 5 lakh shares. The screen captures low-priced, relatively liquid penny stocks that have witnessed significant price declines during the period. (Data Source: ACE Equity).

items.title: IOC, BPCL, HPCL clock Rs 30,106 cr Q2 profit, nearly 39 pc of last year's annual earnings
items.description: In the third quarter, spanning July to September, India's three major state-run fuel retailers announced a combined net profit of Rs 30,106 crore, reversing a previous loss of Rs 18,150 crore. This profitability surge defied the ongoing freeze on petrol and diesel prices since May. Indian Oil Corporation achieved its highest standalone quarterly net profit, buoyed by strong refining margins, yet faces ongoing challenges related to fuel under-recoveries.

items.title: Can Nifty, Sensex extend gains after rallying up to 2% last week? 4 factors to watch on Monday
items.description: Indian benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty ended the week higher, gaining up to 0.5%, even as broader markets declined amid rising crude oil prices above $117 a barrel. Investors will track oil price movements, foreign institutional investor (FII) activity, global cues and domestic market trends for direction. FIIs turned net buyers after a 10-week selling streak, lending support to sentiment.

items.title: FPIs pull out Rs 34,843 cr from equities in Oct; turn net buyers last week
items.description: Amidst rising economic fears, foreign portfolio investors withdrew Rs 34,843 crore from Indian equities in October. Although they had made significant contributions in July and August, outflows continued through September. By late October, a turnaround occurred as foreign investors became net buyers, infusing approximately Rs 6,300 crore into the market. Support from domestic institutional investors provided much-needed stability as all eyes turn to potential global impacts on investor sentiment.

items.title: Nifty IT’s 18% rally may mark a durable leadership cycle; 35,000 next: LKP's Vatsal Bhuva
items.description: Nifty IT’s 18% October rally could signal a sustained leadership cycle, supported by improving momentum, a bullish RSI crossover and capital rotation from global AI stocks. Analyst Vatsal Bhuva sees the index targeting 35,000. He remains cautious on Swiggy, bullish on Acutaas Chemicals, and recommends buying Persistent Systems and Eternal based on positive technical setups.

items.title: Bonus issues, stock splits, dividends: Infosys, Asian Paints among over 40 stocks turning ex-date this week
items.description: More than 40 companies have scheduled record dates for dividends, bonus issues, rights issues and stock splits during November 2–6, 2026. Major names include Infosys, Asian Paints, Coal India, Power Grid and Info Edge, while Sanofi India will offer the week’s highest announced dividend of Rs 75 per share.

items.title: Sebi bars EKI Energy, MD Dabkara, others from market; imposes penalty
items.description: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has taken serious action against EKI Energy Services Ltd and its Managing Director due to financial misreporting. The regulatory body discovered that the company recognized revenue too early and inflated expenses, distorting profit reports. In addition to the company's penalties totaling Rs 88 lakh, several executives were also fined for their complicity in these discrepancies.

items.title: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Monday
items.description: Sensex and Nifty ended the week up about 0.5%, supported by resilient large-cap, IT and healthcare stocks. However, midcap and smallcap indices fell as much as 2% amid rising crude oil prices, inflation concerns and a global technology sell-off.
